summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani specialized in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities, as well as visiting positions abroad.

Aiko Okoshi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral coursework at Kyoto University around 1970–1975 and served as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College, London, and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery before becoming abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.

Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and trained under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah before becoming abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1983.

Ajahn Maha Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2003.

Ajahn Pasanno is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who trained under Ajahn Chah from around 1974 to 1982. He served as the founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Warwick and trained as a disciple under Ajahn Sumedho beginning in 1977, later serving as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies figure who earned an MA at UC Berkeley and studied under Ajahn Chah. He founded Cittaviveka and Wat Pa Nanachat, serving as its abbot in 1975, and was abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held an appointment at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and Honganji Sōgakuin, trained under Gadjin M. Nagao, and held teaching posts at the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, Ryukoku University, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle/University of Paris. He taught at Kyushu University and served as a professor, trustee, vice-president, and center director at Kyoto University.

Akihiro Oda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Otani University. He later held academic appointments there, serving as a lecturer (attested 1992) and Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Akiko Murakawa is an Indology scholar who studied under Harry Falk, Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, Kazuhiko Yoshida, and Muneo Tokunaga.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and served on the faculty at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.

Akio Donohashi specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1968 to 1977 and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Tanabe specializes in Indology and religious studies, earning undergraduate and doctoral degrees from the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Kyoto University, and was appointed professor at the University of Tokyo in 2015.

Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (1931–1934), he held posts there from 1937 to 1968, and held visiting professorships at the University of Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).

Akira Hirakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his degrees at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1975) and taught at Waseda, Rissho, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Akira Miyaji is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his degrees at Nagoya University. He taught at Hirosaki University, Nagoya University, and Ryukoku University, and directed the Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art and Ryukoku Museum.
